claim: Task-relevant practice is associated with musical achievement.
qualifier: Association, not proof that this app causes improvement.

claim: Self-regulated practice includes planning, focused performance, self-observation, and reflection.
sample_or_scope: Survey/review context; advanced Brazilian and Portuguese musicians
qualifier: Do not imply every learner follows the same cycle.

claim: Auditory feedback can support different aspects of musical learning.
sample_or_scope: N=115; 56 guitarists and 59 pianists; four-week protocol
qualifier: Not flute-specific; do not claim measured flute improvement.

claim: Emotion reappraisal, practice hours, and expertise accounted for 26% of variance in self-regulated learning in one professional-musician survey.
qualifier: Research context only; not a consumer promise.

claim: Flute pedagogy commonly addresses tone, breathing, articulation, technique, intonation, and repertoire.
sample_or_scope: NFA pedagogy publications and committee scope
qualifier: Represents recognized pedagogy resources, not a universal curriculum.

claim: Players and flute educators discuss saved tempo settings, tuner/metronome friction, drones, long tones, breathing, and pitch analysis.
qualifier: Qualitative signal; no population estimate; visible social counts are snapshots.

claim: Flute Practice Coach makes a user a better flutist.
qualifier: Requires a controlled product study; never publish as current fact.

claim: The app is designed around evidence-informed practice behaviors.
